title: Loaded besan chilla
summary: Savoury gram-flour pancake that eats like an omelette. Ten minutes, ~18 g of plant protein, and it takes whatever vegetables are dying in the fridge.

ingredients.note: Add slowly - you want thin pouring-cream consistency.
Only if you want them fluffy rather than thin and crisp. Add just before pouring.

steps: Whisk the besan with salt, turmeric and cumin powder in a bowl. Pour in the water a little at a time, whisking, until you have a smooth, thin batter with no lumps. Let it sit 5 minutes if you have them.
Stir in the onion, tomato, chilli, coriander and any greens. The batter should still pour - loosen with a splash of water if the vegetables have thickened it.
Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned pan on medium. Rub it with half a teaspoon of oil.
Pour a ladle of batter into the centre and spread it outwards in a spiral with the back of the ladle. Thinner is better.
Cook 2-3 minutes until the top looks dry and the edges lift. Drizzle a few drops of oil around the rim, flip, and cook another 1-2 minutes until golden.
Repeat with the rest. Eat straight off the pan with curd or green chutney.
tips: Lumpy batter means you added the water too fast. Make a thick paste first, then thin it.
If it sticks, the pan was not hot enough - heat it properly before every chilla.
For a bigger protein hit, whisk 2 tbsp of curd into the batter, or fold in a beaten egg.
health_notes: Besan is about 22 g of protein per 100 g and low-GI, so this holds you far longer than a toast breakfast. No added sugar anywhere.

source.adapted: Standard home recipe, cooked with 2 tsp oil total instead of shallow-frying.
